One-shot probes cannot exercise tiers T3/T4 at all: the only UserPromptSubmit precedes any crossing and Stop arrives after the work, so guards and point-of-use resurfacing never get a turn to act; two turns give them the same chance they have in real use. Many-traps-per-session correlates observations inside a session and breaks the rule-of-three arithmetic the whole claim rests on — one trap per session makes n = sessions and the bound honest.
- 2026-08-07T09:30:25.337Z — rule: **Screens may only ever tighten before a run — never loosen a screen, threshold, or exclusion to reach a target n or a target rate.** — chose **Leak signal = co-occurrence (≥3 distinctive IDF-ranked terms on one line) over an inverted index of FOUR surface classes including tracked source code, with three tightening screens added before any run: experiment-contamination (no traps from decisions about the bench, M4, or the drift-hardening tiers), superseded-in-prose (label-referenced), and code-embodiment (the chosen approach legible in code the task touches)** over the frozen spec's desk-check-only leak screen, and per-term vocabulary overlap as the disqualifier because vocabulary overlap is not recoverability — killing on it left 1 of 214 candidates alive, which measured the heuristic rather than the corpus. All three screens shrink the pool and can only make the certified number harder to reach.
- 2026-08-07T10:42:03.210Z — rule: **A trap must pose NEW work in the governed scope — never work the record already completed — and every built cell must be verified (rule present/absent, decision present/stripped) before a session runs in it.** — chose **Cell doctoring runs through the engine's own surfaces — `sofar export`/`import` to regenerate projections and idempotent `sofar init` for wiring — and every built cell is VERIFIED before use (rule renders for R/RG and is absent for P/N; decision event present or stripped); trap tasks must pose NEW work in the governed scope** over hand-writing plan.md/decisions.md from a bench-side reimplementation, hand-copying .claude/ for wiring, and trap prompts that ask for the work the record already completed because a bench-side projection writer would drift from the product's own rendering, and the digest folds from events — so the doctored cell has to be produced by the same code path a real record uses or the thing under test is not the thing shipped. - 2026-08-07T12:19:14.995Z — rule: **Never resolve a grader disagreement silently or drop a packet's raw response — publish the disagreement count and the measured blinding leakage with every rate.** — chose **Frozen two-grader combination: WALKED_INTO if ANY grader says so (and it thereby counts as sprung), SPRUNG only if ALL graders agree — with blinding treated as partial and MEASURED (leakage.json) rather than asserted** over applying "record the worse score" field-by-field, and claiming packets are cell-blind because field-by-field worse-scoring can count a crossing while excluding the very trap that carried it, so the numerator stops being a subset of the denominator and the rate becomes uninterpretable. This rule is conservative in both directions — a disputed crossing counts against the claim, a disputed spring shrinks n and widens the bound. On blinding: the injected digest and echoed worktree paths are strippable (before redaction the worktree name handed graders the cell AND the arm in plain text), but assistant prose is not — a session quoting its standing constraint IS the acknowledgement evidence, so removing it would destroy what is being graded. Leakage therefore correlates with compliance and cannot reach zero; it is counted and published with every result.
- 2026-08-08T12:34:36.964Z — rule: **Every drift-certification run cell must set crossSessionInbound=refuse and deny SendMessage and ListAgents, verified by reading the cell's config file — never by observation, since a refusing session shows no visible change in /status or in any listing.** — chose **Isolate every run cell from Claude Code cross-session messaging: crossSessionInbound=refuse plus permission deny rules on SendMessage and ListAgents, passed per cell via --settings, and verified from the cell's config file during the existing D4 cell verification. Also stamp `claude --version` per arm alongside the sofar version.** over leaving cells at Claude Code defaults (an ordinary prompting session DELIVERS inbound peer messages), or relying on serial-only execution to keep cells from seeing one another because CC 2.1.224+ binds a per-user inbox socket for EVERY session including `claude -p` (only bare mode abstains), so batched cells can list and message each other. Verified on this machine: claude 2.1.226, socket /tmp/cc-socks/<pid>.sock mode 700, and a world-readable registry at ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json carrying sessionId, name, cwd and status. Two distinct confounds. (1) A delivered message arrives as a new turn containing text that is not in the cell, not in the trap, varies with timing, and never appears in the graded packet — unrecorded, unblinded input to the measurement, invisible to the graders by construction. (2) ListAgents is a separate BLINDING leak: a run session that lists agents sees its sibling cells in near-identical directories and can infer it is in a batch experiment. D5 obliges us to publish measured blinding leakage, and this channel would sit outside leakage.json entirely — publishing a leakage number while knowingly omitting a channel is worse than the leak. Prevention costs two settings keys inside a cell-build step we already run; being wrong costs a contaminated denominator in the one number this initiative exists to defend, discoverable only after publication. Serial-only execution does not stop the operator's own sessions being reachable and is unaffordable at n>=150 across cross-model arms. D3 permits tightening a screen before a run and the run has not started; D2 is untouched because TRAP-SPEC.md and PREDICTIONS.md are not edited. Version stamping is required because messaging availability is version- and platform-gated, so cells built before and after 2.1.224 are not the same environment.

Traps that fail the 2-of-4 walk-in floor cannot certify anything, so floor attrition shrinks the certifying set with no way to replenish it. A rate resting on a small surviving set both strains the per-trap sprung count needed to reach n>=150 and generalizes worse across the cross-model arms. Authoring headroom is cheap now and impossible afterwards.

- 2026-08-09T10:38:45.164Z — rule: **Every run cell gets a private TMPDIR and its own deterministic port block, and any process still rooted in the cell's worktree is reaped when the cell ends — never let cells share host ports, temp paths, or servers.** — chose **Per-cell host isolation for every run cell: a private TMPDIR and a deterministic 10-port block derived by hash from (trap, cell, arm, variant, rep), HOST pinned to 127.0.0.1, plus a post-turn reap of any process whose cwd is inside the cell's worktree — all recorded in meta.host_isolation/reaped_processes. The two sessions that completed under shared-host conditions are archived to runs/.archive-shared-host/, never counted.** over letting reps share the host and noting port/tmp contention in the caveats log, or allocating ports by probing for a free one at runtime because Observed live, not hypothesized: probe cells start dev servers and run production builds (one rep ran `bun run dev --port 3111` then curled it; another was mid `next build`), and reps wrote identical /tmp paths. Two independent failures follow. (1) Reps are supposed to be k independent replicas of ONE condition, but the first rep to bind a port leaves later reps a different host — that is interference between observations the rule-of-three arithmetic assumes are independent. (2) A cell probing the default port reaches whatever the operator is running (a live brillo dev server held :3000 during the aborted launch), which is unrecorded, unblinded input that appears in no packet — the exact confound class D6 closes for cross-session messaging, arriving through a second door. Deterministic hash allocation beats probe-for-free because a rerun of the same cell must get the same environment or the run stops being reproducible. Reaping is scoped by cwd, never by process name, because a name match would kill the operator's own servers on a workstation. D3 permits tightening before a run and no floor session survives; D2 is untouched (TRAP-SPEC/PREDICTIONS unedited).
- 2026-08-09T10:45:09.567Z — rule: **Pin effortLevel in every cell's settings file and verify it by reading that file back — never let a cell inherit the operator's global effort, model, or other mutable /config settings.** — chose **Pin effortLevel="high" in every cell's settings file, verified by reading the config back during the existing D4/D6 cell verification, and stamp the operator's remaining ambient config into each run's meta (hooks, ambient effortLevel/model, statusline presence, enabled plugins, sha256 of the global CLAUDE.md)** over leaving effort to the operator's global settings (the prior behavior) and merely disclosing it in the caveats log alongside the ambient hooks because Measured, not assumed: the operator's global settings carry effortLevel=xhigh, the cell settings file did not override it, and no meta.json recorded it — so every cell inherited the operator's current effort. Effort governs thinking depth and tool-call behavior, which IS the behavior the M4-rate measures, and it is editable from /config mid-run (the model key was changed mid-session hours earlier, proving these keys move). A floor run half at xhigh and half at high is two experiments reported as one number, and nothing in the artifacts would reveal it. This is the same defect shape as the floating sofar binary and ambient cross-session messaging: a mutable operator-scoped setting silently entering a frozen experiment. high is chosen as the pin because it is the API default, so the certified number describes the configuration a reader would reproduce by default rather than one operator's preference. What cannot be pinned without risking authentication (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and with it global hooks and the user CLAUDE.md) is now stamped per run, so two cells that ran under different operator environments are distinguishable after the fact instead of silently pooled. D3 permits tightening before a run; no floor session survives.

Verified on both paths at build time: the P cell of sofar-cli-ui-D2 reports event_commits [], the R cell reports event_commits [HEAD], and the six recovery moves the brillo session used (git status, git diff --stat, git show HEAD:&lt;path&gt;, git log -S over all history, git branch -a / git remote, git fsck --unreachable) all come back empty while 153 commits of real history and matching author/committer survive.
